title: Traffic Phased Rollout Pulse and Risk Log
body:
Purpose:
This doc is the canonical product-ops pulse and risk log for the phased traffic rollout of feature set: adaptive-caching-v2 + prompt-optimizer. Primary goal: provide a short-lived, operational reference that ties traffic phases to KPI thresholds, fast contingency actions, and clear handoff/ownership for day-0/day+7.

Scope / what this covers:
- Phased traffic percentages and timing for Hosted API and Dedicated (pilot customers)
- KPI burnup targets and tolerances used as gating criteria for each phase
- Concrete contingency playbook entries (who does what in first 30/60/120 min)
- Post-launch monitoring checklist and quick-report template for ENG/PD/CS
- Open questions and TODOs before we flip 100%

Quick context / notes to self:
- This is a living doc — will be snapshot into the launch playbook when we go final.
- Related to RDW-4021 (traffic-split infra work) and PRODOPS-8401 (confluence runbook).
- We prioritize SLOs first (latency/availability) then cost KPIs for rollback thresholds.

Milestones (high level)
- M0: Internal smoke (k=0) — feature behind flag, no traffic. (done)
- M1: Canary (1% of new traffic, 10 users) — sanity and early regressions. Target: run 48h
- M2: Pulse (10%) — 24h minimum, compare daily vs control
- M3: Ramp (25% -> 50%) — staged ramps with 6h observation windows
- M4: Full (100%) — monitored 72h with extended 14-day quality checks

Traffic Phases and Gating Criteria (short version)
- Canary (1%):
  - Latency p95 <= 1200ms (hosted), errors < 0.5% over 1h window
  - Model regression: Rouge/BLEU/qual proxy delta <= -2% vs control (sampled prompts)
  - Must pass infra health: no OOMs, no persistent throttling
  - Gate owner: Miguel (eng-infra) + Janelle (prod-ops)

- Pulse (10%):
  - Latency p95 <= 800ms, errors < 0.3% over 6h window
  - Cost/unit delta <= +8% vs baseline OR documented savings due to batching
  - Functional regressions: none with severity >= P1 in sampled evals
  - Gate owner: Aisha (product-ops) + Ravi (platform-eng)

- Ramp (25% -> 50%):
  - Maintain p95 <= 750ms and errors < 0.2% in rolling 6h windows
  - Observability: traces attached for 95% of sampled requests, KV cache hit rate >= target
  - Gate owner: SRE on-call + product-ops lead

- Full (100%):
  - No outstanding P0/P1 regressions in 72h, SLA targets met for committed customers
  - Post-launch quality sample checks completed (see post-launch checklist)
  - Gate owner: Head of Product Ops (Aisha) and Eng manager for serving-runtime

KPI Burnup snapshot (plain text mini-table):
- Metric: Latency p95 (hosted) | Baseline: 620ms | Canary: 580ms | Pulse target: <=800ms | Current: 610ms
- Metric: Error rate (5m rolling) | Baseline: 0.12% | Canary: 0.10% | Pulse target: <=0.3% | Current: 0.11%
- Metric: Cost/1k tokens | Baseline: $1.12 | Expected delta: +6% | Current: $1.18
- Metric: KV cache hit rate | Baseline: 38% | Pulse expected >=45% | Current: 46%

Contingency playbook (fast actions) — prioritized by time horizon
- First 0-15 minutes (triage + quick mitigations):
  1) PD/ENG alerting (on-call) — check error dashboards, top 10 stack traces. Owner: SRE on-call.
  2) If error spike > 0.5% absolute or p95 > 2000ms, flip traffic back to control variant (routing rollback). Owner: Miguel.
  3) If cost surge unexplained (>30% increase QoQ baseline), throttle traffic to 5% and engage infra. Owner: Ravi.

- 15-60 minutes (deeper analysis):
  1) Pull 200 sampled requests + traces, run local repro where possible. Owner: Janelle.
  2) If model output quality regression identified (customer-facing severity), trigger immediate canary halt and notify CS for impacted customers. Owner: Aisha.
  3) Consider auto-deploy fallback model variant (quantized or previous version). Owner: Model ops.

- 1-4 hours (remediation or rollback):
  1) Patch infra config (batching window or mem limits) OR rollback to previous model binary. Owner: infra/serving-runtime.
  2) If rollback, execute post-rollback verification checklist (health, metrics, customer notify). Owner: product-ops.

Pre-launch checklist (must be green before moving to Pulse)
- [ ] All canary instrumentation enabled and validated (traces, logs, metrics) — owner: Miguel
- [ ] Alerts configured with correct thresholds and escalation flows — owner: SRE
- [ ] CS notified of pilot customers and support hours — owner: Sofia
- [ ] Runbook link published to #launch-traffic with on-call roster — owner: Aisha
- [ ] Customer-specific stability checks for Dedicated customers completed — owner: Ravi
- [ ] Baseline synthetic tests executed for 48h and smoke passed — owner: Eng QA

Post-launch monitoring and reporting template (first 12h snapshot)
- 00:00-01:00: Executive pulse (1-liner) — "Live at 10% traffic, p95 610ms, errors 0.11%, no P1" (send to execs & stakeholders)
- 01:00-06:00: Quantitative log (hourly): p50/p95/error-rate/token-cost/KV-hit-rate (paste below)
- 06:00-24:00: Morning handoff summary + decisions on next ramp (yes/no)
- 24h: Full comparison against control + qualitative eval samples (10 random prompts per vertical)

Quick-report example (copyable)
- Subject: Launch Pulse HOUR-06: 10% traffic
- TL;DR: No regressions; latency stable; recommending move to 25% at 2025-03-13T15:00Z
- Key numbers: p95=605ms; errors=0.09%; cost delta=+5%; KV-hit=47%
- Known issues: minor timeout spikes in EU region (investigating)
- Next steps: hold for 6h; SRE to validate EU region network paths; prod-ops to update CS

Handoff and communications
- Who to page for P0: SRE lead -> Eng manager -> VP Eng (on-call rota in runbook)
- Customer notifications: draft template in Confluence PRODOPS-8401 (use only if rollback impacts SSO customers)
- Internal updates cadence: Hourly summaries to #launch-traffic + 2 curated emails to execs at H+6 and H+24

Open questions / TODOs (pre-launch blockers)
- Q1: We still need confirmation that dedicated pilot customers accept a temporary 10% throttled experience during the pulse — @Sofia to confirm with CS by 2025-03-12.
- Q2: Is there a soft-fail for tokenized billing discrepancy? Finance to confirm tolerance (expected +8% cost). Owner: finance (Sam).
- TODO: Add region-level ramp SLOs (APAC/EU/US) — pending infra telemetry doc PR (#678).

Action items (current)
- A1: Miguel — finish canary routing playbook and validate rollback script (due 2025-03-10) — status: done
- A2: Ravi — validate KV cache observability for Dedicated (due 2025-03-12) — status: in_progress
- A3: Janelle — produce 50-sample eval set for quality checks (due 2025-03-11) — status: done
- A4: Sofia — confirm pilot customer opt-in emails (due 2025-03-12) — status: blocked (awaiting list)

Notes / rough thoughts (freeform):
- If we see slow regressions in quality linked to batching, we may need to tune batching window per model size. Noted that smaller contexts are sensitive.
- Keep an eye on tokenization changes when switching model variants — can cause subtle cost/quality shifts.
- Consider an internal "roll-forward" plan where we prefer a tiny model variant with better SLAs over a heavier variant if latency is above threshold.

Appendix: immediate contact list (use runbook page for full roster)
- Product Ops: Aisha Patel (aisha@redwood.ai)
- Engineering infra: Miguel Torres
- Serving runtime lead: Ravi Menon
- SRE: on-call (see runbook)

Last updated: 2025-03-11 by Aisha.

If you're reading this and going to be on-call for the pulse: please add a short note below with availability window and mobile number (helps for quick escalation).
